title: Mobile Gaming May Hurt Your Neck and Elbows
paragraphs: Playing games on your phone can be a fun way to pass the time. However, a new study suggests that people who are addicted to mobile gaming may be more likely to suffer from pain in their necks, backs and elbows.

The study, which was reported in September 2026, surveyed 364 medical students at universities in Jordan. The researchers wanted to find out whether mobile gaming addiction was linked to problems with muscles, bones and joints.

About 9% of the students, or 34 people, met the researchers' criteria for mobile gaming addiction. These students were much more likely to report pain in several parts of their bodies. For example, 85.3% of the students who were addicted to mobile gaming reported neck pain, compared with 65% of those who were not. The difference was even bigger for elbow pain, which was reported by 41.2% of the addicted students, compared with 12.5% of the others. Upper back pain and pain in the wrists and hands were also more common among the addicted students.
In addition, the students who were addicted to mobile gaming were more likely to say that their pain interfered with their daily activities, such as studying and hobbies.

According to the researchers, using a phone for long periods can put strain on the body. This is because people often hold their phones tightly, keep their arms and necks in fixed positions and make the same movements again and again.

The researchers argue that gaming should not only be seen as an issue of screen time or mental health. They recommend that students learn more about good posture and take more breaks. They also suggest that universities could include advice about healthy gaming habits in their health programs.

However, the study had some important limitations. Only 34 students were classified as addicted, and all of the participants were medical students in one country. In addition, the students reported their own pain. Most importantly, the study shows a link between gaming addiction and pain, but it does not prove that gaming causes the pain.
